Cautiously more optimistic. The July 2021 Beige Book points to broad-based increases in hiring and wages and a pickup in tourism in the New York District, reinforcing the FOMC’s July 28 statement that activity and employment continued to strengthen under accommodative financial conditions. These real‑economy gains align with the July 2021 SLOOS, which showed stronger demand for C&I loans across firm sizes, easing terms, firmer consumer credit appetite, and improved qualified‑mortgage demand—supported by better economic outlooks, competition, and strong bank liquidity/capital. While virus-related risks, uneven CRE conditions, and elevated valuations still temper the outlook, the Beige Book’s evidence of labor market firming and services‑sector recovery (tourism) suggests a slightly stronger growth backdrop than previously assessed. Accordingly, sentiment is nudged higher.
